title: fix(runtime)!: dispatchAction runs on the environment's own kernel on a multi-kernel host, and its ai posture answers with the AI door's sentence
body:
Fixes #32055

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — on a multi-kernel host whose `kernel-resolver` throws, `dispatchAction` used to run the call on the host kernel and answer what that kernel answered; it now refuses the call with the resolver's status, as the REST door's scoped path does. No host in this repository registers a `kernel-resolver`, so no in-repo composition's answer moves.
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — `skills/**` never teaches `dispatchAction`, its posture or a `kernel-resolver`; `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx` states both changes.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：宿主 `dispatchAction` 现在用 HTTP 分发器与 REST 门共用的安置步骤（`kernel-resolver` 调用与 scope touch）安置调用：resolver 提示由调用的值写入（`urlEnvironmentId` 只来自宿主指名的 `environmentId`，路由路径只作参考且逐段编码，对象 / 命名空间 / 动作名无法改变 resolver 读到的环境），`environmentId` 由 resolver 写、宿主门不再预写；`ai` 姿态下被拒的客户端动作 / 跨源 api 动作改用 AI 门（MCP `run_action`）原有的拒绝句，不再给出 `target`。文档写明安置之后 REST 门还会做、而宿主门不做的三件事（按所安置 kernel 解析身份、ADR-0069 认证策略门、环境成员门）。
- 为什么改：多 kernel 宿主上，`dispatchAction` 只带 `environmentId` 去问 resolver，读 URL 提示的 resolver 会把调用落到宿主 kernel；resolver 抛错时还会被吞掉、在宿主 kernel 上照跑。REST 门的「直接调用 TARGET」提示写给 REST 调用方，对 agent 没用。契约复审 6784494553 的 F1/F2/F3/F6 在本轮修复。
- 风险与回滚：仓内没有任何组合注册 `kernel-resolver`，单 kernel 宿主答案不变；变化只在多 kernel 宿主——resolver 抛错时由「在宿主 kernel 上照跑」变为按其状态拒绝，这是一次收窄（`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`，changeset 带 BREAKING 与 ADR-0087 处置）。回滚 = revert 本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts`（`placeRequestOnKernel` 与 `placeHostActionRequest`）、`packages/runtime/src/action-dispatch.ts`（`dispatchActionRequest` 的安置步骤、`actionRoutePath`、`aiDoorNotInvokableRefusal`、`dispatchAction` 文档里宿主自担的三项）、`packages/runtime/src/action-dispatch.test.ts`（双 kernel 宿主与「路由路径不可被名字引导」两组钉子）。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/action-dispatch.test.ts src/domains/api-action-forward.test.ts`，预期两文件全绿；把两份源文件换回 base 时，这 7 条钉子里 6 条转红。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

The card comes from the contract review on PR #32032 (record 6757903087). Its two findings, verbatim:

> - **F2, nit.** `dispatchAction` builds its own `HttpDispatcher(kernel)` and a context with no `kernel` and no `dataDriver`, and never runs `resolveRequestScope`. On a single-kernel host this is the REST door's context exactly, which is what the tests prove. On a multi-kernel host the "byte for byte" claim rests on the resolver being registered as the `kernel-resolver` service and honouring a context that carries only `environmentId`; if it yields nothing, the call falls back to the kernel passed in, where REST would have been placed by the resolver first. Nothing in the tree is wrong; the doc does not say which kernel to pass, and no pin covers a resolver. A follow-up card, to settle in cloud's pin round before the mirror is deleted.
> - **F3, nit.** Under `ai`, an entitled agent now receives the REST door's type prescription: for an off-origin `api` action "Call `TARGET` directly (METHOD)", for a client-side action its `target`. Base answered an agent "cannot be invoked via MCP" and named neither. And a never-exposed client-side action is now told to add `ai.exposed`, which could not make it runnable. Still refused, same status. A follow-up card for an `ai`-posture sentence.

**F2, the first arm (resolve the scope the way the REST door does).** `HttpDispatcher.resolveRequestScope`'s environment-and-kernel half is split out in two layers. `resolveRequestKernel` is the REST door's path-parsed hints plus `placeRequestOnKernel`. `placeRequestOnKernel` is the placement both doors share: `kernelResolver.resolveKernel` or `defaultKernel`, then the scope touch. `resolveRequestScope` calls `resolveRequestKernel` first and is unchanged in behaviour. The host door (`dispatchHostAction` -> `placeHostActionRequest`) writes the two resolver hints from the call's values and then runs `placeRequestOnKernel`. `urlEnvironmentId` is the `environmentId` the host named, or nothing. `routePath` is the REST route of the same call as the scoped mount hands it to `dispatch()` (`/actions[/NS]/OBJECT/ACTION`), each segment encoded. No environment hint is ever derived from that path, so the route path the host door builds cannot be steered by an object, namespace or action name. On a host with a `kernel-resolver`, `environmentId` is written by the resolver, never pre-written by the host door, as at the REST door, and a call the resolver places in no environment runs in the kernel's default environment, as the REST door's does. On a host with no `kernel-resolver` nothing places the call, so the host door carries the environment it names exactly as before this change (the scope of the call's service lookups), or the default environment when none is named. It writes that id after placement, so the scope touch still fires only on an id a resolver wrote. A resolver throw leaves through the host door as it leaves `dispatch()`. Before this change, the host door reached the resolver only through `resolveProjectKernelObjectQL`, which carries no hints and swallows a throw into the host kernel. The identity half is not run: the host authenticated its caller, and `executionContext` stays the host's. The REST door's resolver was reachable without touching `action-execution.ts`, so the contract-statement arm was not needed. The doc and type text also say which kernel to pass, and what stays the host's job after placement (below).

**F3.** Under `posture: 'ai'` the type refusal (a client-side action, an off-origin `api` action) keeps its point in the order and its `400`, and answers `Action 'NAME' (type='TYPE') cannot be invoked via MCP`. That is the sentence base MCP `run_action` used, from the invokability refusal in `invokeBusinessAction` before #32032, which `action-dispatch.ts` already carried for the unbound-script refusal. Both sites now read it from one helper, `aiDoorNotInvokableRefusal`, so no third wording exists. The `rest` posture and the REST door keep the prescription. The second half of F3 (a never-exposed client-side action is told to add `ai.exposed`) is gate order, which the card's "What to build" does not take up; it is unchanged.

**What stays the host's job** (contract review 6784494553 F1). `dispatch()` runs three steps after placement that `dispatchAction` does not; the type docs and `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx` now name them. First, resolving the caller's envelope against the placed kernel: `executionContext` is used as given, so it must be the caller as the named environment resolves it. Second, the ADR-0069 authentication-policy gate. Third, the environment-membership gate (`403 PROJECT_MEMBERSHIP_REQUIRED` at the REST door).

Files: `packages/runtime/src/action-dispatch.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts` (outside the claim's file surface, declared here: the extraction of the placement step and the host door's hint writer), the two test files, `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx`, `.changeset/32055-dispatch-action-scope.md`. `action-execution.ts` is not touched.

Ruling hits next to the edits, kept intact: `http-dispatcher.ts` "[#23367, ruling A item 3]" stays in `resolveRequestScope`'s identity half, which is unchanged. The other hits in `action-dispatch.ts` (the ⛔ lines on the envelope, the disabled-object check and the denied-load forward; "ruling B′") are not near the edits.

## Tests

- `action-dispatch.test.ts`, new top-level describe "dispatchAction on a multi-kernel host runs on the environment's own kernel, as the REST door does". It sets up a host kernel that registers `kernel-resolver` and an environment A kernel. The resolver keeps the `KernelResolver` contract: it reads `urlEnvironmentId`, writes `environmentId` and answers A's kernel. The REST door is the real `dispatch()` on `/environments/env_a/actions/...`, with the caller admitted by an `auth` session. Three cases:
  - environment A runs on A's kernel at the REST door's scoped mount (unscoped route path, environment on `request.params`), at its catch-all scoped path and at the host door. The resolver's first question (`routePath`, `urlEnvironmentId`, and the `environmentId` it sees before it writes one) is identical at the scoped mount and the host door;
  - the route path the host door builds cannot be steered by a name: with `environmentId` omitted, an object named `environments`, a namespace named `environments` and an object name containing `/` each leave `urlEnvironmentId` and `environmentId` undefined, and the host kernel is chosen exactly as for a plain name;
  - an environment the resolver does not place runs on the host kernel at both doors (control);
  - a resolver that throws `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` refuses the call at both doors, and nothing runs on either kernel.
- F3: in the `ai` posture group, a url action and an off-origin api action are each refused `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` under both postures. Under `rest` the message equals the REST door's and names the target. Under `ai` it is exactly the AI door's sentence and does not contain the target. MCP case C6 now asserts the AI door's sentence and its equality with the host `ai` answer. In `domains/api-action-forward.test.ts`, the MCP off-origin case now asserts the AI door's sentence instead of the REST prescription.
- Refusal pins assert `status` + `code`. The sentence is pinned where the card asks for the body text.

## Acceptance notes

- Clause-②: the claim said `no`; this PR declares `no (narrowing)`, because one previously accepted call is now refused. Measured: no composition in this repository registers a `kernel-resolver` service (a grep finds only readers), so on every in-repo host the placement step is `context.kernel = defaultKernel` and no answer moves. On a two-kernel host, two answers move. A hint-reading resolver now runs the call on the environment's kernel instead of the host's: a placement change, not an accept-set change. A failing resolver now gets the call refused with its own status (the red leg read base answering `200`, having run on the host kernel): that is the narrowing. The `ai`-posture change is a refusal's sentence only; its status and its point in the order are unchanged. Full dogfood battery: run on the final head, with the counts in the card's report comment.
- Cloud's resolver (`objectstack-ai/cloud`) was not readable from this session, so which reading it uses (hint, header or `environmentId`) is not measured. Since the host door no longer pre-writes `environmentId` on a resolver host, a resolver that reads only a pre-written `environmentId` no longer places host-door calls, as it never placed REST ones; one that reads the scoped-URL hint places both doors' calls.
- Contract review 6784494553 findings F4, F5, F7, F8 and F9 are left as they are, per the fix round.

## Verification

<details><summary>Red leg — the new pins against base source</summary>

`action-dispatch.ts` and `http-dispatcher.ts` checked out from base `e40f2df2` over the committed pins, restored with `git checkout HEAD --` under a trap; `git diff HEAD` empty after. `vitest run src/action-dispatch.test.ts src/domains/api-action-forward.test.ts`: `Tests 6 failed | 109 passed (115)`. The six are the two F3 posture cases, C6, the MCP off-origin case, and two F2 cases. In the first F2 case base gave `{ ran: 'host' }` where REST gave `{ ran: 'env_a' }`. In the failing-resolver case base gave `{ status: 200 }` where `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` was expected. The unplaced-environment control passes on base.
</details>

<details><summary>Fix round ablation — the steering pins</summary>

Ablation 1 (`ablation-replace.mjs`, one-anchor mutation verified landed: blob `b3f95e04` -> `e9e0c934`) puts back path-derived hints on the host door (`this.prepareResolverHints(context, hints.routePath)` in place of `context.routePath = hints.routePath`): `Tests 2 failed | 1 passed` (the two `environments`-name cases). Ablation 2, held with ablation 1, also removes segment encoding: `Tests 3 failed`, the `/`-name case included. Both files were restored: blob equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.
</details>

New pin "dispatchAction on a host with no kernel-resolver keeps the environment the host names": a named `environmentId` is the scope of every scoped service lookup; omitted, it is not.
